scope: Read-only closure review of operation serialization, local TryLock, barrier regressions and child-process contention test.
closed: Both platform TryLock methods now use gate.TryLock before the nonblocking OS call, so a local holder cannot make TryLock block.
The bounded local-holder regression expects false/nil while held and success after release; its failure path releases the holder and collects the worker result.
Serialized waiter test no longer waits for B to reach an OS-lock hook while A owns operation. It checks the operation gate is held, releases A and then collects A/B results.
The Unlock-window test directly observes shared poison inside the seam, releases A before invoking the sibling, and no longer forms the operation-mutex wait cycle.
The child reports actual OS TryLock contention before the release barrier, then acquires the real lock. This removes the former timing-only exclusion assertion.
A single goroutine owns command.Wait; normal completion and forced-termination waits have explicit bounds. No second concurrent Wait is issued.
nonblocking_notes: The in-process fault barrier tests still have bare channel receives and therefore rely on the enclosing test-process timeout if future code fails to reach a barrier. Add per-barrier bounded release/join before broad fault expansion.

If child termination itself exceeds the final bound, the test explicitly fails but cannot prove process exit; t.TempDir cleanup may then encounter an owned live handle. Do not report that exceptional branch as fully recovered. A retained-directory cleanup policy would improve this branch.
limits: No tests, builds or services were executed; this is implementation/test-code review, not a passing execution result.
Approval applies to this tagged catalog slice, not full supervisor/verified-open/bootstrap/cleanup integration or production classroom readiness.
Windows and Unix actual multi-process/death/ACL/durability acceptance remain platform-specific obligations.
